record.paper_title: Open problems in PDE models for knowledge-based animal movement via nonlocal perception and cognitive mapping
record.context_brief: Combining dynamic maps with temporal delays
record.original_question: How can one meaningfully combine a dynamic cognitive map of the kind used in Section 2.2 with either discrete or distributed temporal delays, so that movement is influenced both by an evolving memory field and by explicit reference to past times? In particular, can a standard bootstrapping argument be adapted to prove existence and uniqueness for bounded-domain problems that contain both nonlocal perception and discrete or distributed delays?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 31. How might a dynamic cognitive map interact with distributed or discrete time delays? That is, how might the effects of a dynamic map as found in Section 2.2 combined with discrete or distributed delays as in the models introduced above influence the space use outcomes? Is it possible to use a standard boot-strapping method ... to prove the existence and uniqueness of solutions to problems with both nonlocal perception and discrete or distributed delays in a bounded domain?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an animal population whose density u(x,t) on a bounded domain Ω ⊂ ℝ^n (with smooth boundary and zero-flux, homogeneous Neumann, or homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions) evolves under a reaction–diffusion–advection equation in which movement is biased by both (a) a dynamic cognitive map and (b) explicit dependence on the past. Concretely, let the cognitive map k(x,t) satisfy its own evolution equation coupling memory acquisition, decay, and the current density u, e.g.

  ∂_t k(x,t) = α u(x,t) − β k(x,t) + D_k Δk(x,t),

and let movement of u be driven by a nonlocal perceptual gradient ∇(G ∗ k)(x,t), where G is a spatial detection kernel and ∗ denotes spatial convolution on Ω. Couple this perception with temporal delays of either discrete type, k(x,t−τ), τ > 0, or distributed type, ∫_0^∞ w(s) k(x,t−s) ds, with a non-negative weight w satisfying ∫_0^∞ w(s) ds = 1. The full system reads

  ∂_t u = D Δu − ∇·(u χ ∇(G ∗ K_τ[k])(x,t)) + f(u),
  K_τ[k](x,t) = k(x,t−τ)  or  K_τ[k](x,t) = ∫_0^∞ w(s) k(x,t−s) ds,

together with the cognitive-map equation above, suitable initial history on [−∞,0] (or [−τ,0]), and the chosen boundary conditions.

(i) Formulate a coupled PDE model that meaningfully integrates such a dynamic cognitive map with either discrete or distributed temporal delays, in which animal movement is influenced simultaneously by an evolving memory field and by explicit reference to past times.

(ii) Prove, by a bootstrapping (iterative integration over successive delay intervals) argument or otherwise, existence and uniqueness of solutions to this coupled system on Ω with the prescribed boundary conditions, for suitable classes of initial histories, kernels G and w, and nonlinearities f.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is stated as an open problem in a 2023 survey on PDE models with nonlocal perception and cognitive mapping. Related recent work (e.g., on spatio-temporal dynamics with nonlocal spatial memory and coupled nonlocal PDE–ODE systems with spatial memory) develops well-posedness for either memory or delay components separately, but no source found establishes existence and uniqueness via bootstrapping for a bounded-domain model combining a dynamic cognitive map with discrete or distributed delays. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Open problems in PDE models... (Journal of Math. Biol.)
status_evidence.snippet: Open problems concerning combinations of dynamic cognitive maps with discrete or distributed delays are explicitly listed.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of combining dynamic maps with delays is posed as open.

status_evidence.title: Dynamics of a Coupled Nonlocal PDE-ODE System with Spatial Memory
status_evidence.snippet: Local well-posedness and stability for systems with spatial memory; no explicit delay term combined with dynamic memory map.
status_evidence.claim: Recent well-posedness results address memory or nonlocal perception, but not the combined dynamic-map plus delay setting.

status_evidence.title: Spatio-temporal Dynamics in a Reaction-Diffusion Equation with Nonlocal Spatial Memory
status_evidence.snippet: Analysis of reaction-diffusion equation with nonlocal spatial memory.
status_evidence.claim: Related models handle nonlocal memory but not combined with explicit temporal delays in the cognitive map setting.
